q.q: What is a satellite?
o: An object that orbits a larger object

q.q: What is the Moon?
Why doesn't a satellite fall to Earth?
o: It moves sideways so fast it keeps missing the ground

q.q: Roughly how fast do satellites in low orbit travel?
How high is low Earth orbit?
Which orbit takes 24 hours and stays above one spot?
How high is geostationary orbit?
Which orbit do GPS satellites use?
How long does the ISS take to orbit Earth?
How many times does the ISS orbit Earth each day?
Why can satellite TV dishes point in one fixed direction?
What powers most satellites?
What is a satellite's payload?
o: The instruments that do its job

q.q: Why do satellites need batteries as well as solar panels?
o: For when they're in Earth's shadow

q.q: What does attitude control do?
o: Keeps the satellite pointing the right way

q.q: What does GNSS stand for?
Which country runs GPS?
What is Galileo?
Which is China's satellite navigation system?
What does a navigation satellite broadcast?
o: Its position and the exact time

q.q: How does a receiver work out distance to a satellite?
o: Speed of light × signal travel time

q.q: What is trilateration?
o: Finding position from distances to several known points

q.q: How many satellites are needed for a full GNSS fix?
q.why: Three for position, one for the clock.

q.q: Why is the fourth satellite needed?
o: To correct errors in the receiver's clock

q.q: A signal takes 0.07 s at 300,000 km/s. How far away is the satellite?
About how far wrong would a one-microsecond timing error put you?
q.why: Light travels 300 m in a microsecond.

q.q: Why do navigation satellites carry atomic clocks?
o: Tiny timing errors cause large position errors

q.q: Which systems besides maps rely on GNSS timing?
o: Banks, power grids and phone networks

q.q: Why does GNSS struggle indoors?
o: Weak signals can't pass through buildings

q.q: What is GNSS jamming?
What is GNSS spoofing?
o: Sending fake signals so a receiver thinks it's somewhere else

q.q: How do phones find location when GNSS is weak?
o: They also use Wi-Fi, mobile masts and motion sensors

q.q: What is Earth observation?
o: Gathering information about Earth from space

q.q: What is remote sensing?
Which sensor detects heat from wildfires?
Which sensor works through cloud and at night?
What is a limitation of optical satellite cameras?
o: They need daylight and clear skies

q.q: What is image resolution?
o: The size of the smallest detail an image shows

q.q: Which can a 10 m resolution image show?
What is Copernicus?
Who can use Copernicus Sentinel data?
How do satellites help climate science?
o: Measuring ice, sea level and temperature over decades

q.q: How do satellites help farmers?
o: Spotting crops that need water or fertiliser

q.q: How do satellites help after a flood?
o: Mapping flooded areas to direct rescue teams

q.q: Why is AI used on satellite images?
o: There's too much data for people to check

q.q: Which change could AI spot in satellite images?
Which is a privacy concern about satellite imaging?
o: Very detailed images could show people's homes

q.q: What does a communication satellite do?
o: Receives signals and sends them on

q.q: What is a ground station?
o: A site with antennas for talking to satellites

q.q: What is latency?
Why do geostationary satellites cause high latency?
o: They're very far away, so signals take longer

q.q: About how long does one hop up to a geostationary satellite and down to a ground station take?
o: About a quarter of a second

q.q: Why do LEO satellites give lower latency?
Why do LEO internet systems need thousands of satellites?
o: Each moves quickly and covers a small area

q.q: What is a mega-constellation?
o: Hundreds or thousands of satellites working together

q.q: Which company runs Starlink?
Which is a benefit of satellite internet?
o: Access in remote areas, at sea and after disasters

q.q: Which is a concern about mega-constellations?
Why is control of satellite networks by a few companies a concern?
o: They have a lot of power over important communications

q.q: What new ability do some satellites have?
o: Connecting directly to ordinary mobile phones

q.q: Which option is usually fastest to set up for a remote island's internet?
What is space debris?
o: Human-made objects in orbit that no longer do a useful job

q.q: Which is an example of space debris?
Roughly how many pieces of debris larger than 1 cm may be in orbit?
q.why: Most are too small to track.

q.q: Why is tiny space debris dangerous?
o: It travels so fast it hits with huge energy

q.q: What has damaged ISS windows?
o: Tiny debris such as paint flecks

q.q: What does the ISS do to avoid debris?
What is the Kessler syndrome?
o: A chain reaction of collisions creating more debris

q.q: What could happen if the Kessler syndrome occurred?
o: Some orbits could become unusable for years

q.q: What happened in the 2009 satellite collision?
o: A working US satellite hit a dead Russian satellite
A satellite landed on a house

q.q: Why are anti-satellite missile tests criticised?
o: They create large clouds of debris

q.q: What does deorbiting a satellite mean?
o: Bringing it down to burn up in the atmosphere

q.q: What is active debris removal?
o: Missions that capture and remove junk

q.q: Which is a proposed way to capture space junk?
Why might a laser for nudging debris be controversial?
o: It could be misused as a weapon

q.q: Which helps keep space sustainable?
o: Designing satellites to deorbit after their mission

q.q: What is a CubeSat?
o: A small satellite built from 10 cm cube units

q.q: How big is one CubeSat unit (1U)?
Why can schools and universities afford CubeSats?
o: Standard sizes, off-the-shelf parts and shared launches

q.q: What is a mission objective?
o: The goal the mission aims to achieve

q.q: What is the ground segment?
o: Ground stations, software and people that control the satellite

q.q: Which payload would detect algae in a lough?
How can a CubeSat avoid becoming space junk?
o: Use a low orbit or a drag sail so it reenters within a few years

q.q: What is a spaceport?
Where is the UK spaceport SaxaVord?
Which UK city builds more small satellites than almost anywhere outside the US?
Which job is part of the space industry?
q.why: Most space jobs are on Earth.

q.q: What does a mission operator do?
Which industries use satellite data?
o: Farming, insurance, shipping and climate services

q.q: Why is space law a growing career?
o: Rules are needed for licences, debris and responsible behaviour

q.q: What does a drag sail do?
o: Increases air drag so a satellite falls and burns up sooner

q.q: Which orbit is best for imaging a small area in high detail?
What is a "sun-synchronous" orbit useful for?
o: Taking images at the same local time each day

q.q: Which is NOT a GNSS system?
Why do weather satellites often use geostationary orbit?
o: They can watch the same region constantly

q.q: Which helps rescue services find people when phone networks are down?
What does a 3U CubeSat compare to in size?
Why do operators share satellite orbit data?
What is the main reason the UK cares about space sustainability?
o: It relies on satellites and has companies leading debris removal
